messages:
ci-bot: CI job failed on branch `main` - job `runtime-tests (linux-py3.10)`
ci-bot: failing test: `tests/serve/test_retry_logic.py::test_retry_ordering_non_deterministic`
ci-bot: logs -> https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/1755554321/runtime-tests

maria: @sam heads up — CI turned red, looks flaky (fails ~1/10 runs). Can you retrigger? :eyes:

sam: requeued the job (https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/1755554322). will watch. If it stays flaky we should bisect / run local stress loop.

ci-bot: rerun complete: PASS (flaky pass)

raj: still worth investigating — test asserts ordering of retry events that depend on scheduling jitter. I hit similar locally with `pytest -k test_retry_ordering_non_deterministic -q` and saw occasional failures.

jess: can we add a deterministic seed in the test harness? looks like `random` + `asyncio` scheduling interplay. quick fix: set `random.seed(0)` and `os.environ['PYTEST_RANDOM_ORDER_SEED']='0'` in test setup.

sam: agreed. before we change tests, can someone run a stress loop locally to reproduce frequency? e.g.:

```
for i in `seq 1 200`; do 
  pytest tests/serve/test_retry_logic.py::test_retry_ordering_non_deterministic -q || { echo "FAILED on run $i"; break; }
done
```

raj: ran 200 locally, reproduced at run 27. Attached minimal failing output: 

```
E       AssertionError: expected [A,B,C] but got [A,C,B]
E       assert order == expected_order
E       + expected: [A, B, C]
E       - actual:   [A, C, B]
```

jess: that looks like a race on the retry backoff timers. test uses `retry_backoff_ms = 10` which on CI contended runners isn't stable. Options: increase backoff to 50ms in test, or assert on set membership rather than strict order, or mock the scheduler.

maria: prefer making the test deterministic (seed) or mocking timing rather than widening timeouts which mask bugs. Also we should avoid asserting strict ordering unless ordering is a contract.

sam: I'll start a `git bisect` if it keeps failing in CI. For local quick bisect guidance:

```
# start in a clean repo
git bisect start --bad HEAD --good origin/main~50
# run the stress script in the bisect script target
```

raj: quick note - some recent change to `RetryExecutor` added `asyncio.sleep(0)` to yield. That could change scheduling. @sam can you check the PR range for that change?

sam: yep saw that in PR #1324. I've kicked off a git-bisect run locally pinned to that PR range. Will share results.

ci-bot: CI reported additional flaky failure on a different runner (macos) 2hrs later, same test.

maria: ok plan: (1) sam to finish bisect and share culprit commit; (2) raj to add a repro script that runs the test 500x under `--capture=no` and collects order traces; (3) jess to open a small PR that seeds randomness in test harness + replaces strict ordering with deterministic scheduler mock if bisect points to scheduling change.

sam: bisect narrowed it to commit `f3b2c1a` (PR #1324) — reverting that yields stable passes in my local 500-run loop. PR added the `asyncio.sleep(0)` yield.

raj: nice find. that explains it — the yield changed the micro-ordering but might have exposed a real bug in `RetryExecutor` ordering guarantees. We should either (A) make `RetryExecutor` enforce order under same-priority retries, or (B) make tests less prescriptive.

jess: created GH issue -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/issues/987 (label: flaky-tests, priority: medium). I'll open a follow-up PR with test harness seed and a TODO to address ordering semantics.

maria: thanks team. moving to postmortem if we see more flakes. For now @sam if bisect confirms revert is safe, open a revert PR and we can iterate on a proper fix. :thumbsup:

sam: will do. thanks all.
